models.name: discussion_board_categories
models.description:
Predefined article categories that organize and structure all discussions on the platform.

Stores the fixed set of categories available for article classification: Economics, Politics, Economic Policy, Political Analysis, and Other. Categories define the organizational structure for the entire discussion board, allowing users to browse and discover discussions by topic area.

Categories are foundational reference data maintained by system administrators. Articles must belong to exactly one category. Members cannot create custom categories—only system administrators can add or modify the category list to ensure consistent organization.

Each category includes metadata for display and tracking:
- name: Display name shown to users (e.g., 'Economics')
- slug: URL-safe identifier for filtering and programmatic reference
- description: Purpose and scope of this category
- display_order: Sequence for showing categories in navigation (lower numbers appear first)
- is_active: Whether category is currently available for article selection
- article_count: Denormalized count of published articles in this category (updated when articles are published or archived)

Categories support the discovery workflow by providing a navigation path complementary to search functionality. While not directly transactional, categories are essential infrastructure supporting article organization and member navigation.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Display name of the category shown to users. Examples: 'Economics', 'Politics', 'Economic Policy'. Maximum 50 characters for consistent display in UI.

plainFields.name: slug
plainFields.description: URL-safe identifier for the category used in filtering, search, and API endpoints. Examples: 'economics', 'political-analysis'. Lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens only. Must be unique across all categories.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description of the category's purpose and scope. Explains what types of discussions belong here. Displayed to users when browsing or creating articles. Maximum 500 characters.

plainFields.name: display_order
plainFields.description: Integer sequence number determining category display order in navigation menus. Lower numbers appear first. Categories are sorted by this field for consistent UI presentation. Typical values: 1 (Economics), 2 (Politics), 3 (Economic Policy), 4 (Political Analysis), 5 (Other).

plainFields.name: is_active
plainFields.description: Whether this category is currently available for article selection. Active categories appear in the category filter dropdown and navigation. Inactive categories hide from member selections but retain existing articles. Allows administrators to retire unused categories without data loss.

plainFields.name: article_count
plainFields.description: Denormalized count of published articles currently in this category. Provides quick access for display purposes (e.g., 'Economics (42 articles'). Automatically updated when articles are published or archived. Initialized to 0 when category is created.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when category was created. Records the initial creation time of the category in UTC timezone. Immutable after creation.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to category properties. Updated whenever category name, description, display order, or active status changes. Supports audit trail and change tracking.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when category was soft-deleted. NULL indicates active category. When set, category is hidden from UI but preserved in database for audit trail and historical integrity. Allows category retirement without breaking historical article references.

models.name: discussion_board_system_settings
models.description:
System-wide configuration and settings that control platform behavior and features.

Stores key-value pairs for application configuration, feature flags, and operational settings. Provides centralized management of system behavior without requiring code changes or redeployment. Administrators modify settings through admin panels to control platform features and behavior.

Common settings include:
- Site metadata: site_name, site_description, support_email
- Feature flags: enable_new_user_registrations, enable_comments, enable_file_uploads, enable_search
- Moderation settings: require_article_approval, auto_moderate_comments, spam_detection_enabled
- Rate limiting: max_articles_per_day, max_comments_per_day, max_comment_burst
- System behavior: maintenance_mode, maintenance_message, session_timeout_minutes

Each setting consists of:
- setting_key: Unique identifier for the configuration parameter (e.g., 'maintenance_mode')
- setting_value: The actual configuration value (string format, parsed by application as needed)
- setting_type: Data type hint ('string', 'integer', 'boolean', 'json') helping application parse the value
- description: Purpose and usage of this setting for administrator reference
- is_active: Whether this setting is currently applied; inactive settings are ignored
- updated_by: Moderator or admin who last modified this setting (for audit trail)
- updated_at: When setting was last changed

The system_settings table is the single source of truth for configuration, eliminating the need to modify environment variables or restart the application. Changes are applied immediately or on next request depending on setting type and system design.

All settings are immutable once set—modifications create new entries with updated timestamps rather than overwriting previous values. This preserves configuration history and supports audit trail requirements.

Settings support the operational requirements of the platform by allowing administrators to control feature availability, user behavior constraints, and system maintenance without technical intervention.

plainFields.name: setting_key
plainFields.description: Unique identifier for the configuration setting. Examples: 'maintenance_mode', 'max_articles_per_day', 'site_name', 'enable_user_registrations'. Used by application code to retrieve specific configuration values. Maximum 100 characters. Must be unique combined with category.

plainFields.name: setting_value
plainFields.description: The actual configuration value as string. Format depends on setting_type: boolean settings stored as 'true'/'false', integer settings as numeric strings (e.g., '30'), JSON settings as serialized JSON. Application code is responsible for parsing based on setting_type. Maximum 10,000 characters for complex values.

plainFields.name: setting_type
plainFields.description: Data type hint for parsing the setting_value. Allowed values: 'string', 'integer', 'boolean', 'json'. Helps application correctly interpret the stored value. For example, 'true' string interpreted as boolean true when type is 'boolean'.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Human-readable description of the setting's purpose, usage, and impact. Displayed to administrators in settings management UI to explain what each configuration controls. Helps administrators understand configuration consequences. Maximum 500 characters.

plainFields.name: is_active
plainFields.description: Whether this setting is currently active and applied by the system. Active settings (true) are retrieved and used by application code. Inactive settings (false) are stored but ignored by the application. Allows administrators to disable specific settings without deleting configuration history.

plainFields.name: updated_by
plainFields.description: Identifier of the moderator or administrator who last modified this setting. Used for audit trail to track who made configuration changes and when. Supports accountability and troubleshooting of configuration issues.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this setting was initially created or first recorded. Marks the beginning of this configuration entry for audit purposes. Immutable after creation.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this setting's value or active status. Updated whenever the setting_value, is_active, or other properties change. Helps identify recently modified settings and track configuration changes over time.

models.name: discussion_board_members
models.description: Registered members who can create articles, post comments, and participate in discussions. Members authenticate via email/username and password, undergo email verification before posting access, and can be suspended or deleted. This table represents the core participant base of the discussion board.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Member's email address used for authentication, verification, and communication. Must be unique across all members, valid email format (max 254 characters). Used for account recovery and password reset.

plainFields.name: username
plainFields.description: Member's chosen username for login and public identification. Case-insensitive unique constraint enforced. 3-30 characters, alphanumeric plus underscore/hyphen. Used as alternative login identifier to email.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Bcrypt-hashed password with salt (minimum 12 rounds). Never stored in plain text. Used for authentication during login. Updated when member changes password.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: Public-facing display name shown as author attribution on articles and comments. 1-50 characters. May differ from username for privacy or professional presentation.

plainFields.name: email_verified
plainFields.description: Flag indicating whether member's email address has been verified. False for new registrations. Must be true before member can create articles or post comments. Set to true when verification link is clicked.

plainFields.name: account_status
plainFields.description: Current account status controlling access and permissions. Values: 'active' (normal operation), 'suspended' (temporary restriction due to violations), 'terminated' (permanent ban), 'deleted' (user-initiated deletion). Default: 'active' after email verification.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Account creation timestamp in UTC. Immutable. Recorded when registration is completed.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of last profile or account update. Updated when member modifies display name, bio, profile picture, or other profile fields.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp. Non-null only when account_status is 'deleted'. Used for audit trail and data retention policy enforcement. Allows recovery within 30-day window.

plainFields.name: last_login_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of last successful login. Updated on each successful authentication. Null for never-logged-in accounts. Used for activity tracking and security monitoring.

models.name: discussion_board_member_sessions
models.description: Authentication sessions for verified members. Each session represents a login instance from a specific IP address and device. Sessions track connection context (IP, URL, referrer) for security auditing. Members can have multiple concurrent sessions across different devices. Sessions expire after 7 days or when member logs out.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the member who owns this session. Member's {@link discussion_board_members.id}. Non-nullable (session must belong to authenticated member).

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address (IPv4 or IPv6) from which the login originated. Used for security tracking, fraud detection, and geographic login monitoring.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Full URL/URI where login occurred. Captures the page context of authentication. Used for understanding member access patterns and security context.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: HTTP Referrer header value when login occurred. Indicates which page referred member to authentication. May be empty string if referrer unavailable.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Session creation timestamp (login time) in UTC. Records when this authentication session was established. Immutable.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Session termination timestamp. Non-null when session ends (member logout or expiration). Null for active sessions. Sessions expire automatically after 7 days or when member explicitly logs out.

models.name: discussion_board_moderators
models.description: Administrative users with elevated permissions for content moderation and user management. Moderators authenticate separately from members with their own credentials. Moderators can review pending articles, delete inappropriate content, suspend/ban users, and access moderation dashboards and audit logs.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Moderator's email address used for authentication and administrative communication. Must be unique across all moderators, valid email format (max 254 characters). Typically organizational email for accountability.

plainFields.name: username
plainFields.description: Moderator's username for login and administrative identification. Case-insensitive unique constraint. 3-30 characters, alphanumeric plus underscore/hyphen. Used as alternative login identifier.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Bcrypt-hashed password with salt (minimum 12 rounds). Never stored in plain text. Used for moderator authentication. Moderators may be required to use stronger passwords than members.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: Moderator's display name for identification in audit logs and moderation history. 1-50 characters. Shows publicly in moderation actions (e.g., 'Comment removed by [display_name]').

plainFields.name: account_status
plainFields.description: Current moderator account status controlling access. Values: 'active' (full moderator privileges), 'inactive' (temporarily no moderation access), 'terminated' (permanently revoked moderator status). Default: 'active'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when moderator account was created and role assigned in UTC. Immutable. Records when moderator was granted administrative access.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of last moderator account update. Updated when moderator status changes (activation/deactivation) or password changes.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp. Non-null only when account_status is 'terminated'. Used for audit trail when moderator role is revoked. Allows tracking of when access was removed.

plainFields.name: last_login_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of last successful moderator login. Updated on each successful authentication. Null for never-logged-in moderators. Used for activity tracking and to identify inactive moderators.

models.name: discussion_board_moderator_sessions
models.description: Authentication sessions for moderators performing administrative tasks. Each session represents a moderator login from a specific IP address. Tracks connection context (IP, URL, referrer) for security and audit purposes. Moderators can have multiple concurrent sessions. Sessions expire after 7 days or explicit logout.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_moderator_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the moderator who owns this session. Moderator's {@link discussion_board_moderators.id}. Non-nullable (session must belong to authenticated moderator).

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address (IPv4 or IPv6) from which the moderator login originated. Critical for security monitoring of administrative access and detecting unauthorized login attempts.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Full URL/URI where moderator login occurred. Captures the entry point for moderation dashboard access. Used for understanding moderation access patterns.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: HTTP Referrer header value when moderator login occurred. Indicates source of authentication request. May be empty string if referrer not available.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Session creation timestamp (login time) in UTC. Records when moderator authentication session was established. Immutable. Used for login history tracking.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Session termination timestamp. Non-null when session ends (moderator logout or automatic expiration). Null for active sessions. Sessions expire after 7 days or explicit logout.

models.name: discussion_board_member_profiles
models.description:
Member profile information including display name, bio, and profile picture.

Stores publicly visible profile data for each registered member. Each member has exactly one profile record that is created when the member account is created. Profile information is independent of authentication credentials and can be updated by members at any time.

The profile includes the member's public display name (shown as author attribution on articles and comments), optional biographical information for community introduction, and a URL reference to the member's profile picture. All profile modifications are tracked through timestamps for audit purposes.

When a member account is deleted, the associated profile is also deleted. This separation of profile data from authentication data allows flexible profile management while maintaining data integrity.

foreignFields.name: member_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the member account this profile belongs to. {@link discussion_board_members.id}. Each profile is associated with exactly one member account (1:1 relationship).

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: Public display name shown as author attribution on articles and comments. Required field, 1-50 characters. Used instead of username for public visibility to protect user privacy.

plainFields.name: bio
plainFields.description: Optional biographical information or 'about me' text. Maximum 500 characters. Members can use this to introduce themselves and share relevant expertise or interests related to economic and political discussion.

plainFields.name: profile_picture_url
plainFields.description: URL reference to the member's profile picture. Points to the actual image file stored in the attachment system. Null if no profile picture has been uploaded. Images are automatically resized to 200x200 pixels and EXIF metadata is stripped for privacy.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the profile was created (typically when member account was created). Used for audit trail and member join date tracking. Stored in UTC.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last profile modification. Updated whenever display_name, bio, or profile_picture_url is changed. Used to track profile update history and for audit purposes. Stored in UTC.

models.name: discussion_board_member_preferences
models.description:
Member account preferences and settings for notifications, display, and communication.

Stores personal preference settings that control how members receive notifications, display content, and interact with the platform. Each member has exactly one preference record that stores their individual settings for email notifications, notification frequency, display theme, and other personal preferences.

Notification preferences include options to control email notifications for article replies, comment replies, moderator actions, and optional daily digest emails. Display preferences include theme selection (light, dark, system default). All preferences have sensible defaults to provide a good out-of-the-box experience while allowing members to customize based on their needs.

Preference modifications are tracked through timestamps for audit purposes. These preferences are separate from profile data to maintain clear separation between public identity (profile) and private settings (preferences).

foreignFields.name: member_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the member account these preferences belong to. {@link discussion_board_members.id}. Each preference record is associated with exactly one member account (1:1 relationship).

plainFields.name: email_notifications_enabled
plainFields.description: Master toggle for all email notifications. When false, no email notifications are sent regardless of other preference settings. Default: true to enable notifications. Members can disable to reduce inbox volume.

plainFields.name: comment_reply_notifications
plainFields.description: Whether member receives email notifications when someone replies to their comments. Default: true. Only active if email_notifications_enabled is true.

plainFields.name: article_reply_notifications
plainFields.description: Whether member receives email notifications when someone comments on their articles. Default: true. Only active if email_notifications_enabled is true.

plainFields.name: article_approval_notifications
plainFields.description: Whether member receives email notifications when their submitted articles are approved or rejected by moderators. Default: true. Helps members track publication status of their submissions.

plainFields.name: moderator_action_notifications
plainFields.description: Whether member receives email notifications about moderator actions affecting their content (deletions, edits, etc.). Default: true. Only applies if member's content is actioned by moderators.

plainFields.name: daily_digest_enabled
plainFields.description: Whether member receives optional daily digest emails summarizing new articles and discussions. Default: false (disabled). When enabled, digest is sent daily at a consistent time.

plainFields.name: display_theme
plainFields.description: Preferred display theme for the user interface. Valid values: 'light', 'dark', 'system'. Default: 'system' (follows system preference). Stored as lowercase string for consistent comparison.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when preference record was created (typically when member account was created). All preferences are initialized with defaults at account creation time. Stored in UTC.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last preference modification. Updated whenever any preference setting is changed by the member. Used for audit trail of preference changes. Stored in UTC.

models.name: discussion_board_articles
models.description:
Discussion articles representing the primary content type on the platform. Articles are forum discussion threads initiated by members about economic and political topics. Each article flows through a moderation workflow before publication, requires moderator approval before becoming visible to other users, and supports rich content including text, images, and file attachments.

Articles form the foundation of community discussion. They are the primary business entities that users create to initiate conversations and share perspectives. The article lifecycle includes submission, moderator review, approval/rejection/request for changes, and optional publication. Published articles accumulate comments from community members, creating threaded discussions.

Each article maintains a persistent record even after rejection or archival, supporting audit trails and allowing authors to resubmit rejected content after revisions. Articles reference their creator member, assigned category, and moderation status for proper content discovery and management.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the member who created this article. {@link discussion_board_members.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_category_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the category this article belongs to (Economics, Politics, Economic Policy, Political Analysis, Other). {@link discussion_board_categories.id}

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Article title or headline. Must be between 5 and 200 characters. Serves as the primary identifier for discussion topic and appears in article lists and search results.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Article content body containing the main discussion text. Must be between 10 and 50,000 characters. Supports plain text and basic formatting. This is the core content of the discussion article.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current publication status of the article. Valid values: pending_approval (submitted but not yet reviewed), published (approved and visible to all users), rejected (did not meet guidelines, visible only to creator and moderators), archived (hidden from public view but retained in system). Determines visibility and editing permissions.

plainFields.name: view_count
plainFields.description: Number of times this article has been viewed by any user. Incremented by 1 each time the article detail page is accessed. Initialized to 0 upon creation. Provides engagement metrics.

plainFields.name: rejection_reason
plainFields.description: Text explanation provided by moderator when article is rejected. Helps article creator understand why content did not meet guidelines and what improvements are needed for resubmission. Maximum 500 characters. Null if article has not been rejected.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when article was initially created. Immutable - never changes even if article is edited. Used for chronological sorting and audit trails.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of last modification to article. Updated whenever article content, title, category, or status changes. Used to track edit history and sort by modification recency.

plainFields.name: published_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when article status changed to published (moderator approval). Null if article is not yet published or was rejected. Records the official publication moment for audit purposes.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when article was deleted (soft deletion). Null if article has not been deleted. Enables recovery within retention window and preserves audit trail of deleted content.

models.name: discussion_board_comments
models.description:
Comments represent member responses and engagement on published articles. Comments enable discussion and debate by allowing members to share perspectives, ask questions, and respond to article content. Unlike articles, comments are published immediately without moderation approval, creating immediate visibility and real-time engagement.

Each comment belongs exclusively to one article and extends that article's discussion thread. Comments maintain author information, creation timestamp, and optional attachments (images and files). Comments support editing for content correction and deletion for content removal, with soft deletion preserving comment records for audit purposes.

Comments form the interactive component of the discussion platform, transforming the system from one-way content distribution into collaborative conversation. They are primary business entities requiring independent management through search, filtering, and moderation capabilities.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent article this comment belongs to. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the member who created this comment. {@link discussion_board_members.id}

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Comment text content. Must be between 1 and 5,000 characters. Contains the member's response, perspective, or question about the article. Supports plain text with basic formatting.

plainFields.name: is_deleted
plainFields.description: Soft deletion flag indicating whether comment has been deleted. True if deleted by author or moderator; false if active. Allows recovery of deleted comments for audit purposes while hiding them from user views. Defaults to false.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when comment was originally created. Immutable - never changes. Records the exact moment comment was posted for chronological sorting and rate limiting checks.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of last edit to comment. Null if comment has never been edited. Updated whenever member modifies comment text or attachments. Allows tracking of comment modifications with edit timestamps displayed to users.

models.name: discussion_board_attachments
models.description:
File and image attachments associated with articles and comments.

Stores metadata for all file and image attachments uploaded to articles and comments on the discussion board. Each attachment maintains a reference to its parent content (article or comment) through a polymorphic relationship pattern.

Attachments support multiple file types including images (JPG, PNG, GIF, WebP) and documents (PDF, DOCX, TXT, XLS, XLSX, CSV, ODT, ODS, ODP, ZIP). File validation, malware scanning, and size limiting occur at upload time to ensure security and prevent abuse.

When parent content (article or comment) is deleted, associated attachments are automatically removed from storage. Attachments can be deleted independently by content creators or moderators when removing specific files from posts.

plainFields.name: parent_type
plainFields.description: Type of parent content this attachment belongs to. Either 'article' (references discussion_board_articles) or 'comment' (references discussion_board_comments). Enables polymorphic relationship without multiple nullable foreign keys.

plainFields.name: parent_id
plainFields.description: UUID of the parent content (article or comment) this attachment is associated with. Combined with parent_type to identify the parent entity.

plainFields.name: original_filename
plainFields.description: Original filename as uploaded by the user (max 255 characters). Used for display in UI and download dialog. May contain spaces and special characters.

plainFields.name: storage_path
plainFields.description: System-generated file path where attachment is stored. Uses secure naming pattern (timestamp_hash_originalname) to prevent directory traversal attacks. Unique across entire system.

plainFields.name: file_size
plainFields.description: File size in bytes. Validated at upload time to ensure limits are enforced (10 MB for images, 25 MB for documents). Used for quota tracking and display to users.

plainFields.name: mime_type
plainFields.description: MIME type of the file (e.g., image/jpeg, application/pdf, text/plain). Determined by magic number verification (file header inspection) not file extension, for security.

plainFields.name: file_hash
plainFields.description: SHA-256 hash of file content for integrity verification and malware scanning. Computed at upload time and used to detect file corruption or tampering.

plainFields.name: is_image
plainFields.description: Whether this attachment is an image file. Used to determine display method (embedded inline for images, downloadable link for documents) and whether image dimensions are captured.

plainFields.name: width
plainFields.description: Image width in pixels (for image attachments only). Null for non-image files. Used for display sizing and validation (must be 100-8000 pixels).

plainFields.name: height
plainFields.description: Image height in pixels (for image attachments only). Null for non-image files. Used for display sizing and aspect ratio preservation.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when attachment was uploaded. Immutable after creation. Used for audit trails and display of upload time to users.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of last modification. Updated when attachment metadata is modified. Usually equals created_at except when file is replaced or metadata edited.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when attachment was soft-deleted. Null if attachment is active. Soft deletion preserves attachment record for audit purposes while hiding from user views.

models.name: discussion_board_moderation_actions
models.description:
Comprehensive audit trail of all moderation actions taken on discussion board content. Records every decision to approve, reject, delete, or edit articles and comments by moderators, with full context including reason and detailed notes for accountability and audit purposes.

Captures content review workflow where moderators evaluate submitted articles, approve for publication, request changes, or reject. Also tracks reactive moderation where moderators delete inappropriate comments or articles in response to community guidelines violations.

Each action includes the moderator who performed it, the specific content affected, the type of action taken, and the business reason (rejection reason, deletion reason, edit notes). This immutable record enables tracking of moderation patterns, decision consistency, and provides users with explanation of moderation decisions affecting their content.

Designed as append-only with no updates or deletes - all records preserved for legal compliance, dispute resolution, and system integrity.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_moderator_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the moderator who performed this action. Identifies which moderator approved, rejected, or deleted the content. {@link discussion_board_moderators.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the member who created the content being moderated (article or comment author). Used to track and notify which member's content was moderated. {@link discussion_board_members.id}

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Type of moderation action performed. Valid values: 'approved' (article published), 'rejected' (article not approved), 'requested_changes' (feedback for revision), 'deleted_article' (article removed), 'deleted_comment' (comment removed), 'edited_article' (moderator corrected article content), 'edited_comment' (moderator corrected comment), 'flagged' (marked for further review). Determines business outcome and what notifications are sent.

plainFields.name: content_type
plainFields.description: Type of content being moderated. Valid values: 'article' or 'comment'. Indicates whether action applies to an article or comment to enable polymorphic tracking of moderation across content types.

plainFields.name: content_id
plainFields.description: UUID identifier of the content being moderated. References either discussion_board_articles.id or discussion_board_comments.id depending on content_type value. Combined with content_type, enables tracking moderation across both article and comment entities.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Business reason for the moderation action in 10-500 characters. For rejections: explains policy violation (e.g., 'Personal attacks on individuals'). For deletions: explains violation category (e.g., 'Spam content'). For requested changes: specific feedback (e.g., 'Add citation for economic data in paragraph 3'). Used to notify affected member and maintain moderation consistency.

plainFields.name: notes
plainFields.description: Optional detailed moderator notes up to 1000 characters for internal record-keeping. May contain context about decision (policy interpretation, precedent, escalation factors). Not necessarily shown to user but available to other moderators and administrators for understanding decision rationale.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when moderation action was performed in UTC. System-generated, immutable. Used to order moderation history chronologically and determine time from content creation to moderation.

models.name: discussion_board_user_warnings
models.description:
Audit trail tracking user account management actions taken by moderators including warnings, suspensions, and bans. Maintains immutable record of every disciplinary action, its reason, duration, and auto-reactivation schedule for account lifecycle management.

Records when moderators warn a member about guideline violations (creating accountability for repeated issues), suspend accounts temporarily (blocking posting but allowing viewing), or permanently ban accounts (preventing all access). Each action is timestamped and documented with the moderator name and specific reason.

For temporary suspensions, tracks suspension end date and enables automatic account reactivation when suspension period expires. For permanent bans, records the ban decision with no auto-reactivation. Notifications are sent to affected member explaining restriction reason and duration.

Designed as append-only record for full history of user management actions, enabling moderators to review account history, understand escalation patterns, and make consistent decisions about future violations.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the member account being warned, suspended, or banned. Identifies which user is subject to the moderation action. {@link discussion_board_members.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_moderator_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the moderator who issued the warning or initiated the suspension/ban. Tracks accountability for each account management action. {@link discussion_board_moderators.id}

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Type of user account action taken. Valid values: 'warning' (notification about violations), 'suspension' (temporary block from posting, duration specified), 'ban' (permanent block from accessing system). Determines account restrictions and notification message sent to user.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Required business reason for the action in 10-500 characters. Examples: 'Repeated policy violations', 'Harassment of other members', 'Spam content creation', 'Offensive language'. Explains to member why action was taken and appears in notification email.

plainFields.name: notes
plainFields.description: Optional detailed moderator notes up to 1000 characters for internal record-keeping. May reference specific violations, previous warnings, or escalation factors informing the decision. Available to other moderators for context on account history.

plainFields.name: suspension_end_date
plainFields.description: For suspension action_type only: timestamp when suspension expires and account should automatically reactivate. NULL for warnings and bans (which have no auto-reactivation). Used by system job to auto-reactivate accounts on expiration.

plainFields.name: is_active
plainFields.description: Whether this warning/suspension is currently in effect. TRUE when first issued. For suspensions: changes to FALSE when suspension expires and auto-reactivation occurs. For bans: remains TRUE indefinitely (never auto-reactivates). For warnings: remains TRUE (warnings don't expire, they accumulate in history).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when warning/suspension/ban action was issued by moderator in UTC. System-generated, immutable. Used to order account history chronologically and determine suspension start time.

models.name: discussion_board_reports
models.description:
Member reports of inappropriate content for moderator review.

Members can report articles or comments they believe violate community guidelines. Each report creates a queue item for moderators to investigate and take action. Reports track the reported content, reason for the report, reporter identity, and resolution status.

Reports are distinct from moderation actions. A report is user-generated feedback flagging content; moderation actions are moderator decisions on what to do about reported content. This separation enables tracking both member concerns and moderator decisions independently.

Report status progresses through: pending_review (awaiting moderator investigation) → resolved (moderator took action) or dismissed (moderator determined no action needed).

All reports are permanent records for audit and moderation history purposes.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: The member who filed this report. {@link discussion_board_members.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to reported article (null if report is for a comment). {@link discussion_board_articles.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_comment_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to reported comment (null if report is for an article). {@link discussion_board_comments.id}

foreignFields.name: assigned_moderator_id
foreignFields.description: Moderator assigned to review this report (null until assignment). {@link discussion_board_moderators.id}

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Reason for the report. Predefined values: offensive_language, personal_attack, spam, off_topic, copyright_violation, harassment, other. Helps categorize reports for triage and analysis.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional detailed description provided by reporter explaining why they believe content violates guidelines. Maximum 500 characters. Provides context for moderators during review.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the report. Values: pending_review (awaiting moderator investigation), resolved (moderator took action), dismissed (moderator reviewed and determined no action needed). Used to track report workflow progression.

plainFields.name: moderator_notes
plainFields.description: Notes added by assigned moderator during review. Maximum 500 characters. Records moderator's investigation findings and reasoning for resolution decision.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when report was submitted by member. Used for audit trail and report age tracking.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when report was last updated (status change, moderator notes added, etc.). Tracks modification history.

plainFields.name: resolved_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when report was resolved or dismissed by moderator. Null while report is still pending review. Used to calculate resolution time metrics.
